solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Dishonest dealer in skyscraper, one who moans according to Spooner

indicators.note: Dr Spooner swapped the opening sounds of words, so the starts of the two words are exchanged

parts.note: the Shard is a famous London skyscraper
a carper is someone who finds fault and complains

explanation.surface: A crooked card dealer working in a tall tower whose companion is forever grumbling.
explanation.walkthrough: Swapping the openings of SHARD and CARPER gives CARD and SHARPER.
explanation.definitionFit: A cheat who wins at cards by sleight of hand is exactly a dishonest dealer of the pack.

clue.text: One with the hump about artist? That's sweet

indicators.note: the camel goes around the artist, so one piece wraps the other

parts.note: a camel is the animal famous for its hump
RA is a Royal Academician, a crossword artist

explanation.surface: Someone grumpy surrounding a painter, followed by a chirpy remark that it is lovely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One with the hump' suggests a sulky person, but it is the animal with a hump on its back.
explanation.definitionFit: A toffee-like confection of cooked sugar is a sweet, as a British noun for a candy.

clue.text: Keep talking of game with no name

parts.note: RU is rugby union
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone chattering on about a game that nobody can put a name to.
explanation.definitionFit: To go on speaking at length without stopping is the phrasal verb meaning keep talking.

clue.text: Representative of one dealing in bicycle wheels?

definitions.meaning: someone who speaks on behalf of a group or organisation
read whimsically, a man who handles spokes, the rods of a wheel

explanation.surface: An agent for a firm that sells parts for bikes.
explanation.definitionFit: A person appointed to speak for others is their representative; the second reading splits the word into spokes and man.

clue.text: Missing nothing in something boring

indicators.note: the zero is placed inside the tool, so one piece sits within the other

parts.note: an awl is a tool for boring holes
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: Nothing is lacking in a dull thing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'something boring' sounds like a tedious thing, but it is a tool that bores holes.
explanation.definitionFit: Absent without leave is military slang for a soldier who has gone missing.

clue.text: Earlier test of the country

parts.note: past means earlier, gone by
an oral is a spoken examination

explanation.surface: A previous examination for a whole nation.
explanation.definitionFit: Rural, countryside scenes and life are described as pastoral.

clue.text: Get up and complain having missed golf

indicators.note: something missed is left out, so a letter drops from the word for complain

parts.note: to grouse is to grumble or complain
G is golf in the NATO alphabet

explanation.surface: A golfer who rises and grumbles about skipping a round.
explanation.definitionFit: To wake or rise from sleep or rest is to get up, an old verbal sense.

clue.text: Pensioner told off Queen having adopted son

indicators.note: adopting means taking in, so the son is placed inside the other letters
off suggests something gone wrong, so the letters of told are scrambled

parts.note: ER is Elizabeth Regina

explanation.surface: An elderly man is scolded by the monarch who has taken in his boy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' turns TOLD into OLDT; with ER that is OLDTER, and 'having adopted' puts S in it.
explanation.definitionFit: An informal word for an elderly person, such as someone drawing a pension.

clue.text: Very young scout with story for a convert

indicators.note: one thing put in place of another, so the story replaces a letter

parts.note: Beavers are the youngest section of the Scout movement
a lie is a made-up story

explanation.surface: A tiny scout tells a tale to win someone over to the cause.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for a' says LIE takes the place of the A in BEAVER.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone newly persuaded to a faith or cause is a convert, a person who now has faith.

clue.text: Brag once mob from pub ask all to strip for bitter

indicators.note: stripping each word removes its outer layer, leaving the inner letters of every word

explanation.surface: A boastful crowd at a bar once told everyone to undress, in a sour mood.
explanation.walkthrough: The inner letters RA, NC, O, RO, U and S join up.
explanation.definitionFit: Full of resentment and spiteful feeling, which is what being bitter means.

clue.text: Make a turnover that's somewhat stupendous

indicators.note: only some of the word is used, so a run of its letters is taken

explanation.surface: A business has a remarkable trading turnover.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turnover' sounds like a business's revenue, but here it means flipping something over.
explanation.definitionFit: To turn something upside down is to make it flip over.

clue.text: Like a brother perhaps getting hold of wife's last £500

indicators.note: grasping something means holding it inside, so the letter goes within

parts.note: monky, meaning like a monk, a religious brother

indicators.note: the last letter of the word is taken

explanation.surface: A monastic type takes his late wife's last few hundred pounds.
explanation.definitionFit: In British slang a 'monkey' means five hundred pounds sterling, as a 'pony' means twenty-five.

clue.text: King maybe showing love isn't working

indicators.note: letters put to work in a new order, signalling a rearrangement

explanation.surface: A monarch's romance is shown to be failing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'King' looks like a monarch; it is Stephen King, the horror author.
explanation.definitionFit: Stephen King is an example of a writer of long fiction.

clue.text: Vegetable to stick in shelter

indicators.note: the glue is placed inside the shelter

parts.note: the lee is the side sheltered from the wind
gum is an adhesive used to stick things

explanation.surface: Instructions to wedge a vegetable into a refuge.
explanation.definitionFit: Peas, beans and lentils are pod-bearing plants, eaten as vegetables.

clue.text: Nan's family — and what they might wear

definitions.text: Nan's family — and what they might wear

parts.words: Nan's family — and what they might wear
parts.note: a nanny is a female goat, so her relatives are ..., and the leather they wear is their own hide

explanation.surface: Grandma's relations and the clothes they might put on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nan' suggests a grandmother, but here it is a nanny goat.
explanation.definitionFit: The family of a nanny goat are fellow goats, and the hide they wear is leather from a goat.

clue.text: Minister in hospital ran about, the result of overdoing it

indicators.note: the politician is placed inside the other letters

parts.note: H is the map abbreviation for hospital

indicators.note: about suggests moving around, so the three letters are rearranged

parts.note: Michael Gove, a UK government minister

explanation.surface: A minister rushes around a hospital after drinking too much.
explanation.walkthrough: Michael Gove held several UK cabinet posts; 'about' shuffles RAN to ANR.
explanation.definitionFit: The headache and nausea after excess drinking are the after-effect of overindulgence.

clue.text: Praised first piece of gammon cooked fried with oil

indicators.note: the opening letter of the word is taken
something cooked is transformed, signalling a rearrangement

explanation.surface: Someone lauds a bit of ham fried in oil.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cooked' turns FRIED and OIL into LORIFIED.
explanation.definitionFit: To glorify is to extol or honour, so glorified means extolled.

clue.text: Group of bluesmen playing on base, but not for all

indicators.note: the musicians playing suggests the letters being reworked
excludes a letter from the fodder

parts.note: U is the film certificate for universal viewing, suitable for all
E is the base of natural logarithms

explanation.surface: A band of blues musicians performing on a military base, not for everyone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'but not for all' removes U from BLUESMEN; 'playing' rearranges the rest into ENSEMBL.
explanation.definitionFit: A body of musicians who perform together is a group.

clue.text: Inclination to secure right education

indicators.note: securing means holding something in, so the letter goes inside

parts.note: a leaning is a tendency or inclination

explanation.surface: A preference for guaranteeing a proper schooling.
explanation.definitionFit: Knowledge gained by study is learning, a synonym for education.

clue.text: Swimmer seen in large empty aquarium before game

indicators.note: an empty word has its inside removed, leaving the outer letters

parts.note: game is hunted animals, prey

explanation.surface: A fish spotted in a big empty tank ahead of a match.
explanation.definitionFit: This eel-like jawless fish is an example of a creature that swims.

clue.text: Divine beings enthralling ancient city — they're fruity!

indicators.note: enthralling means holding captive, so the city goes inside

parts.note: gods are divine beings
Ur was a city of ancient Mesopotamia

explanation.surface: Deities captivating an old city, and having a juicy time of it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fruity' hints at saucy, but the definition is literal: these are fruits.
explanation.definitionFit: Hard-skinned fruits of the squash family, so they really are fruit.

clue.text: Mick or Keith, the compiler of this puzzle? Crikey!

parts.note: Mick Jagger and Keith Richards are Rolling Stones
the setter refers to himself as me

explanation.surface: Wondering whether a rock star set this crossword, with an exclamation of surprise.
explanation.definitionFit: A British exclamation of surprise, like 'blimey' or crikey.

clue.text: Trouble Bond's boss's boss about India

indicators.note: the possessive goes around the letter, so one piece wraps the other

parts.note: M is James Bond's boss, with the possessive S
I is India in the NATO alphabet
a chief is a boss

explanation.surface: Spy-world trouble: the head of Bond's chief, in India.
explanation.definitionFit: Mischief is playful naughtiness or harm, i.e. trouble.

clue.text: Person unlucky in love could be this broken

definitions.text: Person unlucky in love could be this broken

parts.words: Person unlucky in love could be this broken
parts.note: a jilted lover is said to be crushed by grief, and the missing organ placed before the word broken gives that state

explanation.surface: Someone crossed in love might be shattered.
explanation.definitionFit: The organ that rules love in idiom; add 'broken' to describe the lovelorn.

clue.text: Old tease provided backing for musical character

indicators.note: backing means going in reverse, so the joined letters are read backwards

parts.note: to rag is to tease
if means provided that

explanation.surface: An old mocker helped fund a stage show's star.
explanation.definitionFit: The barber in Mozart's and Rossini's operas, a character in musical works.

clue.text: Savour memory stifled by teetotallers

indicators.note: something stifled is held in, so the memory sits inside

parts.note: AA is Alcoholics Anonymous
ROM is read-only memory in computing

explanation.surface: Remembered tastes being smothered by abstainers.
explanation.definitionFit: As a noun, a savour is a distinctive smell or flavour, a scent.

clue.text: It's a slight waste, removing lines

indicators.note: letters are taken away from the word for waste

parts.note: slurry is liquid waste such as manure
RY is railway, lines in crosswords

explanation.surface: A small amount of rubbish, with some lines cut out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'slight' looks like an adjective, but it is the noun meaning an insult.
explanation.definitionFit: A disparaging remark or insult is a slight.

clue.text: Roadie regularly cheers accompaniment

indicators.note: taking letters at regular intervals, every other one

parts.note: ta and cheers are both British informal thanks

explanation.surface: A road crew member often shouts encouragement to the backing band.
explanation.walkthrough: 'accompaniment' suggests music, but it is a side dish.
explanation.definitionFit: This yoghurt dish is a side served alongside a curry.

clue.text: Aggressive corporation cut short one company's enquiry, initially

indicators.note: the last letter is removed

parts.note: an old jocular term for a pot belly
I is the Roman numeral one
CO is company, plus the possessive S

indicators.note: the first letter is taken

explanation.surface: A combative firm cut back on a firm's investigation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'corporation' looks like business, but it is old slang for a paunch.
explanation.definitionFit: Bellicose means warlike, keen to fight, so aggressive.

clue.text: Daughter ate out in film

indicators.note: out suggests disorder, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A girl dined away from home while at the cinema.
explanation.definitionFit: The 1967 Mike Nichols movie starring Dustin Hoffman is an example of a film.
